case.source_scope_qualification: Regional historical Brazil Current site means from one published modal processing framework. Moorings have differing noncontemporaneous record windows. DFBS mean flow has specifically low statistical significance. Source mooring positions are nominal; joining them does not recover a physical jet axis or replace the full Brazil Current extent. No snapshot, common-period mean, seasonal range, depth confidence interval, uniform thickness or volume follows.

rules: Use all four published site means, including the explicitly caveated DFBS400m extent. Preserve every contributing site period and reliability flag per sample.
Join nominal Table1 mooring coordinates by WGS84 minor-arc geodesics only as a reference connector. No claim of physical current axis, full-current length or contemporaneous transect.

Interpolate author-reported modal-fit extent descriptors linearly in cumulative connector distance, with50m display rounding and exact anchor values retained. Do not extrapolate beyond the two end moorings.

Provide a separately typed filtered descriptor that is unknown wherever it relies on the specifically low-significance DFBS mean. Filtering must not remove the site and reconnect MARLIM directly toC3. This is a support filter, not an uncertainty interval or proof of greater accuracy.

A five-gravest-mode Gauss-Markov fit to locally rotated record-mean velocities using WOA2009 stratification is not raw instrument-level interpolation or an observation taken in2009. Different site windows must not become continuous1991–2004 sampling or a common annual mean.

Keep Table1 bathymetric depths, the deepest instruments, Figure6 mean fits, Table6 cruise domains/reference isopycnals, transportSv, velocity standard errors and mooring drawdown distinct. None substitutes for physical thickness or supplies a depth confidence interval.
